results.title: A conversation-analytic perspective of repair initiation in ESL ...
results.content: The following research questions guide the study: (1) What repair initiations do teachers and students employ in ESL classroom discourse? This study took place in twenty-six ESL classrooms in the Upper East Region of Ghana using the following research questions: (1) What repair initiation strategies do teachers and students employ in ESL classroom interaction? Since the study is about Repair initiation practices in the ESL classroom, the researchers considered it appropriate to involve only teachers and students. The rest of the study focuses on the verbal and non-verbal repair initiation strategies ESL students and teachers employ to achieve intersubjectivity in classroom discourse. The objectives of the study were to explore repair initiation strategies and examine their functions in teacher-led ESL classroom interactions guided by CA in its methodological approach in senior high schools in the Upper East region of Ghana.

results.title: A conversation-analytic account of student-initiated participation in ...
results.content: This study provides a conversation-analytic examination of student-initiated participation in an English as a Second Language (ESL) classroom, focusing on how such participation occurs in teacher-fronted settings and the role teacher responses play in facilitating or constraining further student talk. Verplaetse (Eds.), Second and foreign language learning through classroom interaction (pp. As Rod Ellis states in his Preface, Craig Chaudron's book, Second Language Classroom: Research on Teaching and Learning, published in 1988, reviewed systematically the L2 classroom research up to that time. Although Chaudron updated the research community on the development of classroom research in 2001 with an article published in The Modern Language Journal, the space given to it and the relatively brief nature of the review make it necessary that a new volume presenting a comprehensive survey and critical appraisal of the research into L2 learning and teaching in classrooms be available. Descriptive research discussed in this chapter range from interaction analysis to classroom discourse analysis, types of language use, conversation analysis and the L2 classroom, and scaffolding in sociocultural theory.
